newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weak, July hits one-month low.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weak, July hits one-month low.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures tumbled on Wednesday, with July breaking through a key support level to reach a one-month low.
July softened in the morning on fund liquidation and some producer hedging in back-month March. But sales picked up when New York gapped lower at the open and broke crucial support at $1,440.

Once that level in New York broke, traders said technical sales by funds kicked in to drag CSCE July down through its next support at $1,425 and push London's July down to the lowest level since May 6.
The contract also suffered on rollovers into September, traders said, and the July/September spread continued to widen. At the close, the spread stood at 22 stg compared with 21 on Tuesday.

July recovered off its session low to end down 23 stg at 994 stg per tonne. September lost 22 to 1,016. Total volume stood at a healthy 10,139 contracts, with July notching the top spot with 4,240 lots changing hands. September followed with 2,668 contracts.

After the day's action, traders said cocoa was technically weak with more sales expected before first notice day in New York on June 17. Those sales should also keep prices under pressure in the near-term.
If CSCE July breaks $1,410 or if London slips below the April 9 low of 980 stg, traders said fresh sales could emerge and spin cocoa into a downward spiral.
If July slipped further, support was not seen until the 950- to 930-stg area, traders said.
Initial resistance was now pegged at July's old support base near 1,000 stg.
